question: Under OC 186A, are PoS tap payments for merchants or person-to-person transfers?
actual_response: Under OC 186A, UPI Tap & Pay transactions on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.

question: Summarise OC 186A, covering the requirements across its sections.
draft_reference: Cover the source-supported requirements across all cited pages; report incomplete coverage explicitly.
actual_response:
Circular OC 186A, titled 'Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)', was issued by NPCI on September 10, 2026, to extend UPI Tap & Pay via NFC from QR codes to PoS terminals for contactless payments.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are restricted exclusively to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the feature, while also providing users the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals within their acquiring network.
Device lock must be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per-transaction limit is capped at INR 5000, above which additional authentication factors may be required.
UPI Application Providers must present UPI Tap & Pay as a standalone feature via a dedicated call-to-action, not embedded within other services or menus.
Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for these transactions must follow extant UPI guidelines, along with RBI guidelines on Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation.
Remitter Banks must validate the user's account for feature enablement before processing each transaction, while users can set their own limits within the INR 5000 ceiling.
Detailed functional, technical, and operational requirements are to be found in applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Documents, Technical Specifications, and other NPCI instructions issued from time to time.

question: Compare OC 186 and OC 186A: Attribute original NFC capability and later device-lock requirements separately.
draft_reference: Attribute original NFC capability and later device-lock requirements separately.
actual_response:
OC 186 (issued 2023-12-19) attributes the original NFC capability requirement to mobile devices having NFC capability and operating on Android or iOS systems.
OC 186A (issued 2026-09-10) introduces later device-lock requirements, mandating that a device lock be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay and ensuring the device is in an unlocked state at the time of initiating a transaction.
